findings.statement: Q4 fail (capability-overclaim): the new row gitlab-project-token-tier is `verified`, but its statement includes a property nobody has proven: 'so gitlab-issues/gitlab.com/rest-v4 needs no paid subscription'. Its evidence is a single documentation read, and its `source` points to the design §5.6 instead of the GitLab documentation. Two separate claims share one verified status: the measured fact (project access tokens require Premium/Ultimate on GitLab.com) and an inference about the profile (a free-tier personal access token with `api` scope can run the whole provider suite).
findings.evidence: assumptions.yaml:55-57: status: verified; statement ends '...member of the target projects only, so gitlab-issues/gitlab.com/rest-v4 needs no paid subscription.'; source: docs/superpowers/specs/...#56-profils-exacts-visés. Roadmap §6 (plans/2026-10-24-v1-roadmap.md:469) calls only the tier fact 'confirmée' and records the token choice as an owner decision. It says nothing about the profile working without a subscription. provider-matrix.yaml:8 keeps the GitLab profile `unresolved`, so no qualification backs that clause. Fix: drop the 'so ... needs no paid subscription' clause, or move it to its own `assumed` row that reopens on the first GitLab qualification. Point `source` to the GitLab documentation page.

findings.statement: Q5: the corrected GitLab cell adds 'au rôle minimal', which is not in the owner decision recorded in the roadmap. The roadmap says only 'compte de service dédié, membre des seuls projets cibles'. The addition is consistent with the design's minimal-scope principle (§2), but it goes beyond the 2026-10-24 decision and does not match provider-matrix.yaml:8 or ADR-0006:148-150, which both omit it.
findings.evidence: design:406 '... membre des seuls projets cibles au rôle minimal ...'; roadmap:469 '... compte de service dédié**, membre des seuls projets cibles (`auth.mode: personal-access-token`, `scopes: ["api"]`)'.

findings.statement: Q1: D4 adds a rule that neither the design §4 nor the roadmap contains: 'A feature that helps the reporter but weakens a rule the buyer set is refused.' It is attributed to owner decision D4 with no source. The rest of D4 is faithful ('Politique, audit et reçus sont le cœur produit').
findings.evidence: design:169 D4 consequence: 'Politique, audit et reçus sont le cœur produit'. ADR-0006:44-46 adds the refusal sentence. grep of the design and roadmap finds no equivalent.

findings.statement: Q1: two owner decisions of 2026-10-24 sit under the heading 'D12 — One deployment per customer, one organization per deployment': the GitLab.com personal access token and the reception page's transport check with the server's verifyExport verdict. Neither follows from D12. Each bullet does carry an explicit '(owner decision of 2026-10-24)', so they stay traceable, but the placement suggests they come from D12. The D12 consequences themselves (one signing key per deployment, roles from the customer's OIDC) are faithful.
findings.evidence: ADR-0006:135-154; design:177 D12 consequence: 'Une clé de signature par déploiement, rôles issus de l'OIDC du client (§5.7)'.

findings.statement: Several decisions in the accepted ADR are agent choices that design §9 lists as 'choix de l'agent à vérifier à la lecture': WASM rather than FFI (Proof component), author/approver separation, origin typed by the person, OAuth/App profiles excluded, the managed browser policy rejected. The ADR header credits the whole decision to 'owner decisions D4 to D13' and never marks these as agent choices that the owner endorsed through the design approval. decision-lock policy-receipt-wasm-component (decision-lock.yaml) is `verified` on this basis.
findings.evidence: design:511-528 §9 lists 'crate Rust compilée en WASM...', 'séparation auteur / approbateur...', 'profils à jeton plutôt qu'OAuth/App'. ADR-0006:4-6 'Decision owner: owner decisions D4 to D13'. ADR-0006:65-67, 167-173, 236-242.

findings.statement: Grammar: 'the destinations the matched rules explicitly denies' should read 'deny'.

Test gap: the new tests check how the four v1.0 provider rows bind to their profiles, but never that those rows stay `unresolved` (or at least not `verified`/`qualified`). No test checks that the new card criteria are `pending` either. Q3/Q4 hold today only by inspection. A later edit that promotes a row would pass both test files.
findings.evidence: qualification-v1.test.ts:34-41 compares only `row?.profile ?? statement prefix`. project-card.test.ts has no assertion on `status`.

limitations: Q1 pass apart from F3-F5: D5 through D13 each appear in ADR-0006 with a consequence that matches design §4. The rule precedence, retired keys staying in the exported set, strict Ed25519 verification and Jira `lookup: unsupported` come from roadmap §4.1, §4.2 and §6.

Q2 pass: ADR-0005:66 contains the design §5.2 phrase word for word ('voluntary active-tab capture, observed origin retention, and gesture-bound delivery to one configured origin'); the design wraps it across lines 290-292 and the text is identical once whitespace is normalized.

Q3 pass: the card criteria are policy-routing, signed-receipt-offline, gesture-bound-delivery and stale-plan-refused; two-real-profiles and browser-matrix-real are extended; the kill predicate is destination-disclosure-leak. All are `pending`. The count of 'status: accepted' is 3 before and after. maturity (specified) and exposure (spec-published) are unchanged.

Q4: the four v1.0 provider rows are `unresolved`. Each statement starts with its exact profile id (github-issues/github.com/rest-2022-11-28, gitlab-issues/gitlab.com/rest-v4, jira-cloud/cloud/rest-v3, plane/self-hosted/rest-v1). The binding is a statement prefix, not a structured field; the `profile` field arrives with L5 (roadmap §4.5). The new decision-lock rows are `verified` in the existing sense of 'decision recorded in an ADR', the same as the pre-existing rows. They are not evidence of implementation. The only overclaim is F1.

Q5 pass apart from F2: the design status matches the merged ADR-0055 (PR #134, merged 2026-10-23T07:03:02Z by the owner account, D94 in DECISION-REGISTER.md), and Annex A quotes ADR-0055 D1 verbatim. Note: the Statut line of ADR-0055 still reads 'proposed — la fusion de cette pull request par le propriétaire constitue l'arbitrage', and it carries no dated arbitration line. The 'gel levé' claim rests on that ADR's own rule that the merge is the arbitration.
Q6 pass: neither the diff nor the commit messages add a dated Owner-arbitration marker. The only occurrences are the existing prose 'l'agent n'écrit jamais de ligne `Owner-arbitration:`'.

This review does not prove any provider qualification (GitHub, GitLab.com, Jira Cloud, Plane), any browser qualification, or the validity of any documentation measurement dated 2026-10-24 (GitLab tier, Atlassian search and reconcile). The reviewer did not re-read those external documents.
This review is not owner consent or owner arbitration, and it cannot stand in for them. ADR-0006 says 'accepted', and the review cannot confirm that the owner endorses that status before the merge.
Gate discrimination (neutralization of the new tests) was not exercised. The gates were run once, read-only, on HEAD.
The plan files for each lot (for example L0 task 7B/7C) and the implementers' reports were not read: the reference set was limited to the design, the roadmap and ADR-0055.
